//: Forbidden regions — predicates over ACCUMULATED session state, not over any single action. This is the whole point: a per-action classifier is structurally blind to these because the hazard is a property of what the session has assembled, not of the current call. A region is a conjunction of effect flags that must never all hold at once on a path that crossed no gate. Kinds are closed: safety | ordering.

regions.name: lethal-trifecta
regions.gloss: external content + readable secrets + a live outbound channel, all held at once — the combination where instructions from that external content could carry a secret off the machine. You've declared this should never be reachable without a gate.

regions.name: credential-egress
regions.gloss: secrets readable and an outbound channel live at once — a secret could leave the machine. Does not need an external trigger (it also covers a tool or MCP server acting on its own). The path to credential egress, stated in one line.

regions.name: source-egress
regions.gloss: first-party source is readable and an outbound channel is live at once — code can leave the machine. This is NOT a credential leak; it is a different loss (your own source / IP). It is the one the credential-shaped defenses miss: a model primed to refuse '.env exfiltration' and a classifier tuned for secret patterns both see 'read a .js file, POST it somewhere' as ordinary work — because nothing here looks like a secret. The policy permits it all the same.
